To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully prepared a novel graphene-based composite catalyst, which exhibited excellent electrocatalytic performance for methanol oxidation.

a novel sandwich-like graphene/carbon nanosphere/graphene (rGO/CNS/rGO) composite was successfully prepared by a facile one-pot solvo-thermal method, and the Pt3Ni nanoparticles loaded on the rGO/CNS/rGo substrate exhibited superior catalytic activities in methanol oxidation.
we developed a one-pot synthesis of Pt3Ni/rGO catalysts with high activity and durability for methanol electrooxidation by using carbon nanospheres as a support.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple, one-pot solvo-thermal approach to the fabrication of sandwich-supported Pt3Ni nanoparticles for the electrooxidation of methanol.

the development of novel graphene/carbon nanosphere/graphene sandwich supported bimetallic catalysts with excellent electrocatalytic performance, which could be extended to other bimetallic nanoparticles and graphene derivatives.
a new strategy for preparing highly active and stable Pt3Ni alloy electrocatalysts for methanol oxidation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the one-pot solvo-thermal process in N,N -dimethylformide without any reducing agent and surfactants is a simple and facile method for the synthesis of graphene/carbonate nanospheres/graphen sandwich supported Pt3NI nanoparticles with enhanced electrochemical properties in methanol oxidation, which may provide a new route to prepare other graphene-based nanocomposites for electrocatalytic applications.

the Pt3Ni nanoparticles anchored on the carbon nanosphere/graphene sandwich substrate exhibited excellent electrocatalytic performance in methanol oxidation, which is attributed to the synergistic effects of the Pt3 Ni nanoparticles and the sandwich-like structure.

the sandwich-like graphene sheets/CNS/graphene sheets structure not only prevented the restacking/refolding and aggregation of graphene sheets, but also enhanced the electron transfer between the catalyst and the electrode, which resulted in the superior electrochemical performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sandwich-like graphene sheets/CNS/graphene sheets substrate is an effective support material for Pt-based electrocatalysts, and the Pt3Ni/CNS/rGO catalysts are highly promising for use in fuel cells and direct methanol fuel cells.
the sandwich-like graphene sheets/carbo nanospheres/graphenes sheets substrate could be used as a promising support for the preparation of highly active electrocatalysts for methanol oxidation.
the Pt3Ni nanoparticles can be well dispersed on the sandwich-like graphene sheets, which can be used for the electrochemical detection of methanol.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the one-pot solvo-thermal method can be used to fabricate graphene/carbon nanosphere sandwich supported Pt3 Ni nanoparticles with enhanced electrochemical activity and durability for methanol oxidation.
